newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines Imelda's jewellery to be auctioned.
newsitem.headline: Philippines Imelda's jewellery to be auctioned.

text.p: Some $12 million in jewellery once worn by former Philippine first lady Imelda Marcos will soon be auctioned off and the proceeds used to aid landless Filipinos, a senior government official said on Friday.

Final details of the auction, including security provisions, are being finalised with Sotheby's auction house, but the government hopes to complete the sale by year-end, Magtanggol Gunigundo told Reuters in an interview.
"We have not yet decided on the (venue), whether it will be in London, Manila or Switzerland," said Gunigundo, head of the Presidential Commission on Good Government.
The Philippine government is also finalising an indemnity agreement protecting the jewellery from loss.
"Supposing there is a hijacking of the items in transit? We would like to be indemnified right away," Gunigundo said.
Sotheby's appraisers have vauled the jewellery at around $12 million, and the proceeds will finance a government programme aimed at providing land for poor agricultural workers, he added.

Gunigundo's commission is trying to recover the wealth that Imelda Marcos, her late husband Ferdinand and their associates are accused of illegally acquiring during their 20-year rule. It has so far recovered more than $1 billion, he said.

The jewellery is in three collections. The first was left behind when the Marcoses fled the Malacanang presidential palace in Manila in 1986 after a popular uprising, and the second was confiscated from them when they arrived in Hawaii.
Ferdinand Marcos died there in exile in 1989.
The third collection was seized from a Greek national trying to leave the Philippines from Manila international airport. The Greek claimed it was his, but a court ruled it was Marcos loot.
The gems are in a vault in the Philippine Central Bank.
